title: Welcome to the 2026 EEID Workshop
text:
Find out more about the workshop and its leaders on the About page.
For topics and timings, check out our Schedule page.
Information about pre-workshop preparation is available on the Materials page.

title: Materials for the EEID Workshop 2026
text:
We will be using R for all data manipulation and analyses/model fitting. Any operating system (Windows, Mac, Linux) will do, as long as you have R (version 3.6 or higher) installed.
We will be using RStudio to run R.
We will host all materials on GitHub. All students need a GitHub account as that is how we will share materials.




For this workshop, we assume basic familiarity with:

Basic R Programming Language
Basic calculus including functions
Basic probability and statistics

Review of R

A great short refresher on R is the Biological Computing in R Chapter in The Multilingual Quantitative Biologist.
Some resources for brushing up on R:


The Multilingual Quantitative Biologist
Code Academy
Data quest

Review of Calculus

There are many on-line tutorials. One resources with some good videos is 3blue1brown.
A concise cheatsheet summary can be found under `A Complete Calculus Cheatsheet’ at Paul’s Online Notes

Review of Probability and Statistics
There are many on-line tutorials. One resources with some good videos is 3blue1brown.

title: About the EEID Workshop 2026
text:
The 2026 EEID associated workshop will be an Introduction to Spatial Modeling.
The workshop will be taught by

Lauren Childs
Kate Langwig
Angela Peace
Michael Robert
Nick Ruktanonchai
Omar Saucedo

The EEID Workshop will involve collaborative sessions with the Vectorbyte Training Workshop.
